chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I fear that I will perform the qunut while there are those who differ from me behind me.' He said, 'Your raising of your hands suffices,' meaning raising both of them as if you are bowing (in ruku').
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on raising hands during qunut if followers differ?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a practical concession for the qunut supplication, ruling that simply raising the hands is sufficient even if the congregation behind the imam does not follow suit. By equating the hand-raising gesture to the bowing (ruku') position, he emphasizes the validity of the individual act of devotion regardless of communal uniformity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of sunnah practices in prayer. This ruling underscores the principle that the imam's personal adherence to recommended acts does not obligate the followers to replicate every detail, thereby preventing unnecessary confusion or division within the prayer row.
